deep.reconstruction:
Context. Cote 154 deals with 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of pseudolines in the projective plane. In modern terms these are closely related to rank-3 oriented matroids, Goodman–Pollack 'allowable sequences' and wiring diagrams. On the preceding pages Grothendieck builds several 2-dimensional cell complexes ('cartes', i.e. combinatorial maps / surfaces): X_0, X_1, X'_1, X_2, X_3. They model a fixed configuration X with its system Σ of pseudolines D_i and the 'positions relatives' (superposed, critical, supercritical) of two pseudolines D_i, D'_i.

The variants differ in several ways:
- Some have cusps ('pointes') on the boundary and some do not.
- In X_3 the pseudoline D_i is replaced by a Möbius band, which is a tubular neighbourhood of a pseudoline in RP^2.
- X'_1 gives a differentiable representation of (X, Σ), whereas X_3 only gives a representation of a convex tubular neighbourhood of Σ in X.
- For X_3 Grothendieck notes that the singular faces do not come from a single combinatorial source. So X_3 does not admit an interpretation in terms of the internal combinatorics of the local system of the polygons Pol(D).

What this page (numbered 6') adds:
1. Coverings. For each of the five maps there are principal coverings with group the dihedral group D_{2n}, associated to the Pol(D).
   - Pol(D) is presumably the 2n-gon attached to the n pseudolines (the cyclic order of their 2n 'ends', or of the directions).
   - These Pol(D) form a local system over the map, with monodromy in the symmetry group D_{2n} of the 2n-gon.
   - The associated principal D_{2n}-bundle (the 'frame bundle' of the polygon local system) gives coverings X̃_i.
   - These are ramified over the first three maps (X_0, X_1, X'_1) and presumably unramified over X_2, X_3.
   - Grothendieck calls the X̃_i the 'déploiements ultimes' (ultimate unfoldings): the monodromy of the polygon is fully trivialised on them.
2. Choice of models. The most useful models seem to be X'_1, X_2, X_3 and their coverings. He hopes X_2, X_3 and their tilde versions can be dispensed with in favour of X'_1 and X̃'_1, provided X'_1 embeds in X as planned.
3. Doubt. He then says he is not fully convinced, as he does not see how to handle the neighbourhood of the boundary in a 'supercritical' manner. The reading of these lines is uncertain.

Overall the page is a methodological stock-taking: a list of candidate combinatorial/topological models, the dihedral 'unfolding' coverings, and a preference with a caveat. The right half of the sheet is recycled computer listing paper (JESNEWS, Cadarache, August 1982) with no mathematical content.
errors: No mathematical claims are proved on the page, so there is nothing to check rigorously.

Unclear point: ramification of a principal D_{2n}-covering 'sur les trois premières' cartes is only meaningful if, for X_0, X_1, X'_1, the polygon local system degenerates at some cells (cusps or boundary). That is plausible given the cusped boundaries, but it is not explained here.
The order convention for D_{2n} (order 2n versus symmetries of a 2n-gon, order 4n) is ambiguous on the page.

ideas.what: Combinatorial cell-complex models ('cartes') of a pseudoline configuration and its relative positions, in several variants (with or without cusps; pseudolines thickened to Möbius bands).
ideas.modern_name: Cellular / zonotopal models of pseudoline arrangements; Möbius-band neighbourhoods of pseudolines in RP^2; wiring diagrams
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (1926), Ringel (1956), Goodman–Pollack (1980s), Folkman–Lawrence (1978) for topological representation

ideas.what: Principal D_{2n}-coverings (possibly ramified) of these maps, associated to the local system of polygons Pol(D); called 'déploiements ultimes'.
ideas.modern_name: Frame bundle / monodromy covering of a local system of polygons with dihedral structure group; analogous to cyclic/dihedral covers of configuration spaces and to sweeps / allowable sequences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Closest are Goodman–Pollack allowable sequences (periodic 2n-sequences with dihedral symmetry); no exact counterpart known

ideas.what: Methodological choice: prefer the smooth model X'_1 and its covering, provided it embeds suitably in X.
ideas.modern_name: Choice of a smooth versus combinatorial model

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes dihedral (D_{2n}) principal coverings, ramified over some models, of combinatorial surfaces attached to a pseudoline system, as the 'ultimate unfoldings' trivialising the local system of polygons Pol(D). This topological/monodromy viewpoint on pseudoline arrangements (local systems, ramified coverings) is not standard in the oriented-matroid literature, which is mostly purely combinatorial.
missed.quote: il y a pour chacune les revêtements de ces cartes (ramifiés sur les trois premières) principaux du groupe D_{2n}, associés aux Pol(D) - Ce sont ces revêtements X̃_i qui sont les déploiements ultimes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could link pseudoline arrangements and allowable sequences to monodromy and covering theory of their cell complexes, in the spirit of dessins and cellular maps. This is of modest interest, but it documents a geometric approach to rank-3 oriented matroids that was never pursued.

missed.claim: There is an unresolved question whether the smooth model X'_1 embeds in X compatibly with the boundary (supercritical) structure, which would make X_2 and X_3 unnecessary.
missed.quote: Peut-être pourra-t-on se passer des X_2, X_3 et leurs tildés, au profit des X'_1 et X̃'_1 ... je n'en suis pas tout à fait convaincu
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it is a technical step in his programme, but it is an open thread within the notes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a planning and survey page within an unpublished, little-studied project on pseudolines. The dihedral 'déploiement' coverings are an unusual topological viewpoint, but they are only named, not developed. The page contains no finished result.
transcription_corrections: Line 'et tant[?] que X_1 s'insère' is more likely 'et pourvu/tant que X'_1 s'insère' (the image shows a prime on X_1).

'du coup[?], [-ayant quelques-] {+en voyant+}' is probably '- je n'en suis pas tout à fait convaincu, ne voyant pas comment ...' with the deleted phrase 'ayant quelques' and the inserted 'un voisinage' above the line.
The final word is likely 'supercritique' ('d'une façon supercritique'), consistent with the vocabulary of the previous page.
In 'associés aux Pol(D)' the group symbol is written as a double-struck D with subscript 2n, as transcribed.
